arxiv-2006-09270.title: Primal Dual Interpretation of the Proximal Stochastic Gradient Langevin Algorithm
arxiv-2006-09270.creator: Adil Salim, Peter Richtárik
arxiv-2006-09270.description: Abstract We consider the task of sampling with respect to a log concave probability distribution. The potential of the target distribution is assumed to be composite, i.e. , written as the sum of a smooth convex term, and a nonsmooth convex term possibly taking infinite values.

arxiv-2103-11697.title: Random-access quantum memory using chirped pulse phase encoding
arxiv-2103-11697.creator: James O’Sullivan, Oscar W. Kennedy, Kamanasish Debnath, Joseph Alexander, Christoph W. Zollitsch, Mantas Šimėnas, Akel Hashim, Christopher N. Thomas, Stafford Withington, Irfan Siddiqi, Klaus Mølmer, John J. L. Morton
arxiv-2103-11697.description: Abstract As in conventional computing, memories for quantum information benefit from high storage density and, crucially, random access, or the ability to read from or write to an arbitrarily chosen register. However, achieving such random access with quantum memories in a dense, hardware-efficient manner remains a challenge.

arxiv-2201-09091.title: Target Sensing with Intelligent Reflecting Surface: Architecture and Performance
arxiv-2201-09091.creator: Xiaodan Shao, , Changsheng You, , Wenyan Ma, , Xiaoming Chen, , and Rui Zhang
arxiv-2201-09091.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xiaodan Shao, , Changsheng You, , Wenyan Ma, , Xiaoming Chen, , and Rui Zhang. Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has emerged as a promising technology to reconfigure the radio propagation environment by dynamically controlling wireless signal’s amplitude and/or phase via a large number of reflecting elements. In contrast to the vast literature on studying IRS’s performance gains in wireless communications, we study in this paper a new application of IRS for sensing/localizing targets in wireless networks.

arxiv-2401-17520.title: On the Fourier coefficients of powers of a finite Blaschke product Thanks: The work of R.Z. was supported by the pilot center Ampiric, funded by the France 2030 Investment Program operated by the Caisse des Dépôts.
arxiv-2401-17520.creator: Alexander Borichev, Karine Fouchet, Rachid Zarouf
arxiv-2401-17520.description: Abstract . Given a finite Blaschke product B B we prove asymptotically sharp estimates on the ℓ ∞ \ell^{\infty} -norm of the sequence of the Fourier coefficients of B n B^{n} as n n tends to ∞ \infty . We provide constructive examples which show that our estimates are sharp.

arxiv-2402-14175.title: Towards Contact-Aided Motion Planning for Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots
arxiv-2402-14175.creator: Priyanka Rao, Oren Salzman, and Jessica Burgner-Kahrs
arxiv-2402-14175.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Priyanka Rao, Oren Salzman, and Jessica Burgner-Kahrs. Tendon-driven continuum robots (TDCRs), with their flexible backbones, offer the advantage of being used for navigating complex, cluttered environments. However, to do so, they typically require multiple segments, often leading to complex actuation and control challenges. To this end, we propose a novel approach to navigate cluttered spaces effectively for a single-segment long TDCR which is the simplest topology from a mechanical point of view.

arxiv-2404-04356.title: Pixel-wise RL on Diffusion Models: Reinforcement Learning from Rich Feedback
arxiv-2404-04356.creator: Mo Kordzanganeh, Danial Keshvary, Nariman Arian
arxiv-2404-04356.description: Abstract Latent diffusion models are the state-of-the-art for synthetic image generation. To align these models with human preferences, training the models using reinforcement learning on human feedback is crucial. Black et. al 2024 introduced denoising diffusion policy optimisation (DDPO), which accounts for the iterative denoising nature of the generation by modelling it as a Markov chain with a final reward.

arxiv-2410-02021.title: On the Resilience of Fast Failover RoutingAgainst Dynamic Link Failures
arxiv-2410-02021.creator: Wenkai Dai, Klaus-Tycho Foerster, Stefan Schmid
arxiv-2410-02021.description: Abstract Modern communication networks feature local fast failover mechanisms in the data plane, to swiftly respond to link failures with pre-installed rerouting rules. This paper explores resilient routing meant to tolerate ≤ k \leq k simultaneous link failures, ensuring packet delivery, provided that the source and destination remain connected.

arxiv-2501-09614.title: Exploring the wettability of liquid iron on refractory oxides with sessile drop technique and density-functional derived Hamaker constants
arxiv-2501-09614.creator: Sudhanshu Kuthe, Mathias Boström, Wen Chen, Björn Glaser, Clas Persson
arxiv-2501-09614.description: Abstract The macroscopic interactions of liquid iron and solid oxides, such as alumina, calcia, magnesia, silica, and zirconia manifest the behavior and efficiency of high-temperature metallurgical processes. The oxides serve dual roles, both as components of refractory materials in submerged entry nozzles and also as significant constituents of non-metallic inclusions in the melt.

arxiv-2501-13136.title: Forecasting of Bitcoin Prices Using Hashrate Features: Wavelet and Deep Stacking approach

arxiv-2501-13136.description: Abstract Digital currencies have become popular in the last decade due to their non-dependency and decentralized nature. The price of these currencies has seen a lot of fluctuations at times, which has increased the need for prediction. As their most popular, Bitcoin(BTC) has become a research hotspot.

arxiv-2504-05787.title: Finiteness properties of asymptotically rigid handlebody groups
arxiv-2504-05787.creator: Sergio Domingo-Zubiaga
arxiv-2504-05787.description: Abstract . We introduce asymptotically rigid mapping class groups of handlebodies and determine their finiteness properties, which vary depending on the space of ends of the underlying handlebody. As it turns out, in some cases, the homology of these groups coincides with the stable homology of handlebody groups, as studied by Hatcher and Wahl.

arxiv-2510-04930.title: Egalitarian Gradient Descent: A Simple Approach to Accelerated Grokking
arxiv-2510-04930.creator: Ali Saheb Pasand, Elvis Dohmatob
arxiv-2510-04930.description: Abstract Grokking is the phenomenon whereby, unlike the training performance, which peaks early in the training process, the test/generalization performance of a model stagnates over arbitrarily many epochs and then suddenly jumps to usually close to perfect levels. In practice, it is desirable to reduce the length of such plateaus, that is to make the learning process ”grok” faster.

pmc-10674308.description: South Africa has a dual high burden of HIV and drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). This was a retrospective chart review of 246 patients who began treatment at two DR-TB hospitals in Eastern Cape, South Africa between 2017 and 2020.

pmc-10740942.description: Simple SummaryThe field of veterinary minimally invasive surgery has grown, but there is a lack of easily accessible training tools for practitioners worldwide. Some simulators are being developed, validated, and found to be effective for training vets both in basic skills and advanced techniques.

pmc-11356254.creator: Ruqing Ye, Xiaoming Chen
pmc-11356254.description: Electromigration (EM) is a critical reliability issue in integrated circuits and is becoming increasingly significant as fabrication technology nodes continue to advance. The analysis of the hydrostatic stress, which is paramount in electromigration studies, typically involves solving complex physical equations (partial differential equations, or PDEs in this case), which is time consuming, inefficient and not practical for full-chip EM analysis.

pmc-11522277.title: Comparative analysis of aldosterone and renin assays for primary aldosteronism screening
pmc-11522277.creator: Yuki Taki, Takashi Kono, Kyoko Teruyama, Takamasa Ichijo, Ikki Sakuma, Hidekazu Nagano, Hiroka Miyagawa, Satomi Kono, Masanori Fujimoto, Naoko Hashimoto, Masataka Yokoyama, Eiryo Kawakami, Takashi Miki, Tomoaki Tanaka
pmc-11522277.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The transition from radioimmunoassay (RIA) to chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassay (CLEIA) for plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) assays has raised concerns over its impact on primary aldosteronism (PA) diagnosis. This study investigated the correlation between PAC and renin values using RIA, CLEIA, and liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS), established cutoff values for PA diagnosis using the aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR) with PAC_CLEIA, and assessed the differences in PAC values by measuring weak mineralocorticoids (WMs).

pmc-13170012.title: Fasciitis of the Breast, Ranging from Necrotizing to Non-Necrotizing Forms: A Diagnostic Dilemma Necessitating Vigilant Clinical Scrutiny
pmc-13170012.creator: Safna Naozer Virji, Sahra Mateen, Alisha Fatima Rizvi, Lubna Mushtaque Vohra
pmc-13170012.description: SUMMARYNecrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rare but highly aggressive infections characterized by rapid necrosis of the skin, subcutaneous tissue, and fascia. While typically seen in the abdomen, perineum, and extremities, NSTIs of the breast are uncommon and often misdiagnosed as cellulitis, mastitis, or abscess, contributing to delayed treatment and high morbidity and mortality.

pmc-13223149.title: From health protection to labor incentive: health and economic impacts of Medical Financial Assistance in rural China
pmc-13223149.creator: Yarong Wang, Weikun Yang, Shi Yin
pmc-13223149.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Medical Financial Assistance (MFA), a key safety net for low-income groups in China, may exert incentive or welfare dependency effects on non-farm labor supply, an issue critical to assessing the effectiveness of medical security policies. Using two-wave household panel data, this study employs two-way fixed effects models to evaluate MFA’s impact on the non-farm labor supply (participation rate and working time) of low-income rural households, distinguishing between the effects of eligibility attainment and increased assistance amounts.

pmc-13408562.title: New records of extinct Icacinaceae from Paleocene rainforests of northwestern South America
